short: Social support, loneliness and Internet addiction

items.label: Research purposes
items.prompt: The research purposes are listed (a)–(d). Find purpose (d), the one about MEDIATION.
items.model: Does loneliness mediate the relationship between social support and Internet addiction?
items.why: Purposes are listed at the end of the 'Overview of the Present Research' section, not at the end of the Introduction.

items.label: Purpose (a)
items.prompt: Find purpose (a).
items.model: Explore the relationship between the three dimensions of social support and loneliness over time.
items.why: '…we put forward the following research purposes: (a)…'

items.label: Hypotheses?
items.prompt: Does the article state formal directional hypotheses before the Method?
options: Yes, a hypothesis is stated for each path
No, only purposes are listed (though the Method mentions 'hypotheses')
Yes, but only for loneliness as a mediator
items.ans: No, only purposes are listed (though the Method mentions 'hypotheses')
items.model: No formal hypotheses, only purposes (a)–(d). The analysis section still mentions 'the aforementioned hypotheses', which is inconsistent.
items.why: Spotting this kind of inconsistency is part of critical reading.

items.label: Mediator
items.prompt: Which variable is tested as the MEDIATOR, and at which time point was it measured?
items.model: Loneliness, measured at T2 (6 months).
items.why: A mediator sits between predictor and outcome in time: social support (T1) → loneliness (T2) → Internet addiction (T3).

items.label: Conceptual definition (loneliness)
items.prompt: Find the conceptual definition of LONELINESS.
items.model: A subjective feeling that arises when a person senses a lack of satisfactory relationships and a gap between desired and actual communication.
items.why: It's in the literature review, not the Introduction.

items.label: Conceptual definition (Internet addiction)
items.prompt: Find the definition of INTERNET ADDICTION the authors adopt.
items.model: 'Compulsive overuse of the Internet and irritable or moody behavior when deprived of it.'
items.why: They first note that many competing terms exist, then choose one.

items.label: Conceptual definition (subjective support)
items.prompt: Social support has three dimensions. Find the definition of SUBJECTIVE support.
items.model: The subjective and experiential emotional support of individuals.
items.why: Objective support, subjective support and support utilisation are defined in separate sentences.

items.label: Competing theories
items.prompt: Find the sentence summarising the THREE competing views about loneliness and Internet addiction.
items.model: Internet addiction causes loneliness; loneliness causes Internet addiction; or they influence each other.
items.why: Rather than one framework, the authors set up competing explanations that a cross-lagged design can compare.

items.label: Research gap (design)
items.prompt: Find the limitation of previous studies that explains why a LONGITUDINAL design was needed.
items.model: Most earlier studies were cross-sectional, which can show correlations but not causal direction.
items.why: The 'Limitations in Previous Researches' section lists the gaps as First, Second.

items.label: Research gap (dimensions)
items.prompt: Find the gap about the DIMENSIONS of the variables.
items.model: Few studies explored loneliness, the 3 dimensions of social support and the 4 dimensions of Internet addiction together.
items.why: Several gap sentences exist; this one summarises the dimension gap.

items.label: General method
items.prompt: Which best describes the design?
items.model: Three waves over one year (T1, T2 at 6 months, T3 at 1 year); no manipulation.
items.why: Longitudinal = the same people measured repeatedly; still correlational because nothing was manipulated.

items.label: Sampling
items.prompt: Find the sentence stating the SAMPLING method.
items.model: Cluster random sampling at a postsecondary school in Shandong, China.
items.why: Sampling method is the first sentence of Participants and Procedure.

items.label: Final sample
items.prompt: Find the sentence giving the FINAL sample size.
items.model: 169 students (88 girls, 81 boys; mean age 18.31).
items.why: 214 responded at T1, but dropout and invalid responses reduced it to 169.

items.label: Attrition check
items.prompt: Find the sentence describing how the authors checked whether DROPOUTS differed from those who stayed.
items.model: Independent t-tests comparing participating and non-participating adolescents (none significant).
items.why: If dropouts differed, the final sample could be biased.

items.label: Measurement timing
items.prompt: Find the sentence stating WHEN each variable was measured.
items.model: Social support and Internet addiction at T1 and T3; loneliness at T2.
items.why: The order of measurement is what allows the mediation test.

items.label: Reliability problem
items.prompt: Find the sentence (in the Method) showing that the social support subscales had LOW reliability at T1.
items.model: T1 α = 0.67 total; subscales 0.67, 0.62, 0.61 (below the usual .70).
items.why: Alphas below .70 are often considered weak; the authors admit this in the limitations.

items.label: Model fit
items.prompt: Find the sentence reporting that the model fitted the data well.
items.why: Compare with the criteria in the Method: CFI/TLI ≥ .90 is acceptable; RMSEA .05–.10 is 'basically acceptable'.

items.label: Mediation result
items.prompt: Find the sentence reporting the significant INDIRECT (mediated) effects.
items.model: E.g., OS (T1) → loneliness (T2) → CIU & WIA (T3), indirect effect −0.07, 95% CI −0.13 to −0.02.
items.why: An indirect effect is significant when its confidence interval does not include 0.

items.label: Overclaiming causation
items.prompt: Find the sentence where the authors claim their aim was to ESTABLISH CAUSATION, something a correlational design cannot do.
items.model: 'A key objective… was to establish causation using cross-lagged regression coefficients…'
items.why: Cross-lagged designs show temporal order, but without manipulation they cannot establish causation. Hedged wording like 'predict' would be more appropriate.

items.label: Practical implication
items.prompt: Find the practical recommendation for PARENTS OR SCHOOLS.
items.model: Increase first-year students' social (especially emotional) support and interpersonal skills to prevent Internet addiction.
items.why: Implications are in their own section.

items.label: Limitation (self-report)
items.prompt: Find the limitation about COMMON METHOD BIAS.
items.model: All variables were self-reported, which may inflate correlations (common method bias).
items.why: When everything is measured the same way, shared method variance can make variables look more related than they are.

items.label: Future research
items.prompt: Find the suggestion to collect data from OTHER SOURCES.
items.model: Collect data from teachers, parents or classmates to verify the findings.
items.why: This addresses the self-report limitation directly.
